Article Title: Disha Salian death case: CBI registers FIR, takes over probe from Mumbai Police
Article Text:
The court had criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR despite the investigation continuing for nearly six years

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Monday registered an FIR in connection with the death of Disha Salian, former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput , days after the Bombay high court ordered a central agency probe into the case.The FIR follows the high court's September 2 order directing the CBI to register a case and conduct a fresh investigation into Salian's death. The court had criticised the Mumbai Police for failing to register an FIR despite the investigation continuing for nearly six years, observing that it "raises more questions than answers".The bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and Ranjitsinha Raja Bhonsale had said a case investigation could not continue for an inordinately long period and directed the CBI to appoint a suitably experienced and senior officer to investigate the matter.The court also directed the Mumbai Police to hand over all case papers to the CBI and record the statement of Salian's father, Satish Salian. It made clear that registration of the FIR did not mean that anyone would automatically be treated as an accused."Nobody shall be treated as an accused unless, in the opinion of the investigating officer, there are sufficient grounds to raise reasonable suspicion against him depending on the material collected during the investigation," the court said.Salian, 28, died on June 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in Mumbai's Malad area. Mumbai Police had registered an Accidental Death Report (ADR) and, following an inquiry, concluded that her death was a suicide.The high court pointed to what it described as "glaring discrepancies" in the police investigation, including the timing of the spot panchnama and questions concerning injuries sustained by Salian.Salian's father had approached the high court alleging that his daughter was raped and murdered and seeking a CBI investigation. He had also sought an FIR against Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, though the high court refrained from making findings against any individual.Salian had briefly worked as Rajput's manager. Rajput was found dead at his Mumbai residence on June 14, 2020, six days after Salian's death. A separate CBI probe into Rajput's death was ordered, with the agency later filing a closure report stating that he died by suicide.
Article Summary: The bombay high court ordered a central agency probe into the case. The court had criticised the mumbai police for failing to register an fir. Disha salian, 28, died on june 8, 2020, after falling from a residential building in mumbai's malad area.

Article Title: Ex-Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal surrenders before Goa court in 2013 rape case

NEW DELHI: Former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal surrendered before the Mapusa court on Monday after the Bombay high court sentenced him to 10 years in prison for raping a junior colleague in a hotel lift in Goa in 2013.Tejpal had challenged the high court’s verdict in the Supreme Court , which directed him to surrender within two weeks. The high court’s ruling on August 6 overturned his acquittal by a Goa sessions court in 2021 and convicted him of the offence.The Supreme Court’s direction means Tejpal must begin serving his sentence, subject to any further orders in his appeal.The case relates to allegations that Tejpal sexually assaulted a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in November 2013 during an event organised by Tehelka magazine.A Goa sessions court acquitted him of all charges in May 2021, saying the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The Goa government challenged that decision before the Bombay High Court, which later overturned the acquittal and imposed a 10-year rigorous imprisonment sentence.Tejpal approached the Supreme Court through advocate Aditya Samaddar. The Goa government has also challenged the high court’s sentence, seeking life imprisonment on the grounds that the punishment was inadequate considering the seriousness of the offences.
Article Summary: Former tehelka editor-in-chief tarun tejpal surrendered before the mapusa court on monday. Bombay high court sentenced him to 10 years in prison for raping a junior colleague in a hotel lift in goa in 2013. Supreme court directed him to surrender within two weeks.

NEW DELHI: The BJP and the Congress , two arch political rivals, sparred over Rahul Gandhi 's student-outreach event, "Chhatron Ki Goonj", with Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav dubbing it "Jhooth Ki Goonj" (echo of lies).Striking a combative note over the Madhya Pradesh CM's remark, senior Congress leader PC Sharma said: "They kept calling him 'Pappu', but now he has become everyone's 'Papa'."The verbal clash ensued after CM Mohan Yadav attacked the entire Gandhi-Nehru family, saying: "Why is it that Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi, Rajiv Gandhi, and others in later times never contested elections from Delhi? They do not contest from Delhi because the people there know them too well. People joke that the only reason he didn’t go to Arab to contest elections is that the ocean stood in the way."He further said: "They seek out other places because they only need to face the public once every five years; they have no intention of actually working for the people. That is why, every time, they come up with new lies..."PC Sharma hit back at Mohan Yadav's remark, saying: "Ever since Rahul Gandhi visited Jantar Mantar to speak up for the youth, the BJP has been anxious across the country"."The leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party are unaware of the history of the freedom struggle and why elections are contested from Raebareli... Mumbai: Union home minister Amit Shah said Sunday that all 21 NDA-governed states would implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) before 2029. Triple talaq has been abolished, giving Muslim women equal rights. We have introduced UCC in several states and I am confident that in the 21 BJP-NDA-governed states, we will introduce UCC before 2029," he told reporters here.Asked whether the 1951 baseline would be used for implementing National Register of Citizens in Manipur, Shah said the Centre is holding discussions with allies and political parties over it. "Whatever decision is taken, we will inform you," he said. He said govt had ended five decades of Maoism and signed over 14 peace agreements in the the northeast region. "More than 9,000 people have surrendered and today we have taken the Northeast on the path of development. "Home Minister Amit Shah refused to disclose the methods being deployed to identify illegal Bangladeshi migrants and their detection in cities such as Mumbai. “You are asking the home minister to make the tools public and tell you how it will be done. The minister reiterated the government’s resolve to identify and deport infiltrators from the country.On the national security front, Shah said the dilution of Articles 370 and 35A of the Constitution had been achieved without a single drop of blood being shed or a bullet being fired, and asserted that Kashmir was now fully integrated with India. The home minister said surgical strikes, air strikes and Operation Sindoor had established a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism.Asked whether a white paper would be released on the Rs 25,000-crore Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank scam case, involving the late Ajit Pawar, Deputy CM Sunetra Pawar and their nephew NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar, amid conflicting findings by state and central agencies, Shah said agencies were doing their work. the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1947, when present-day Uttarakhand was also part of the state."As the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh... he initiated efforts to present the Article Title: Murder accused takes out 'victory march' after bail, SC tells Haryana cops to produce him in court

NEW DELHI: Taking a stern view of a murder accused taking out a "victory procession" on being granted bail by Punjab and Haryana HC, Supreme Court has directed Haryana Police to produce him before it.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta also recorded in its order that despite a non-bailable warrant being issued against the accused, he had not been produced in custody.The matter was taken up for hearing on Sept 8.Taking note of the counsel's submission that the accused, Vishal, had held a procession after getting bail and threatened witnesses, the bench directed the accused to surrender. "We will hear you once you surrender and then seek bail. Taking out a victory procession on bail is not right," it said.It noted that the non-bailable arrest warrant issued in Aug has not been executed and the accused has not been arrested by the police. It added that the warrant could not be executed for reasons which the court was not going into at present."However, we direct the superintendent of police, district Charkhi Dadri, Haryana to ensure that the warrant is executed and respondent is produced before this court on the next date, which is being fixed as Sept 21, 2026," SC ordered.It directed the registry to forward a copy of the order to the SP within 24 hours.The high court granted bail to the accused in the murder case on April 23.An altercation took place between the accused and family members of the complainant, Rajbala, on Oct 27, 2022 after Vishal allegedly started constructing tin sheds on a disputed plot of land. During a heated exchange, Vishal allegedly hit several people with lathi and axe, grievously injuring several persons belonging to the complainant's side, one of whom died.Following this Vishal was arrested and kept in custody for over three years.The HC rejected Vishal's bail petition four times but accepted it the fifth time after it was pointed that material witnesses have been examined in the case and he has spent over three years in custody. Article Title: Elephant Madhuri now on her way to Kolhapur as Anant Ambani's Vantara vows continued medical care
Article Text: Madhuri, the elephant popularly known as Mahadevi in Kolhapur, will be allowed to return to the city after the High-Powered Committee (HPC) passed an order on September 9, Anant Ambani’s Vantara said in a statement on Thursday.According to Vantara, the HPC permitted Madhuri’s return after hearing the parties' claims, reviewing reports, and inspecting the facility at Nandani in Maharashtra. The order has laid down several conditions, including that Madhuri cannot be used in processions or for any other purpose.The elephant will also need round-the-clock care and a medical examination every fortnight, Vantara said.Madhuri was brought to Vantara in Jamnagar on July 30, 2025, in compliance with directions from the HPC, which the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court upheld. Vantara said it had not sought her custody but had received and cared for her in accordance with the directions.The organisation said Madhuri’s health had stabilised after sustained veterinary care, but her chronic conditions still require supportive management and regular monitoring.As part of the transition, Vantara said it had helped arrange living conditions, veterinary infrastructure, medical equipment, medicines and other necessities at the Nandani facility. Its veterinarians will visit Madhuri in Kolhapur every fortnight to conduct her medical examination and submit reports to the competent authorities, as directed by the HPC.Vantara also said it had worked to improve the enclosure at Nandani within the available infrastructure. Further upgrades, it said, were currently restricted by town-planning constraints, including a road passing through land belonging to the trust.The organisation added that it would remain available to support future upgrades at the facility and would assist if directed by the courts or competent authorities.“Madhuri’s wellbeing remains Vantara’s first concern. Our commitment to her health, welfare and dignity does not depend on where she lives,” the statement said.
Article Summary: Madhuri, the elephant popularly known as mahadevi in kolhapur, will be allowed to return to the city. The high-powered committee (hpc) passed an order on september 9, anant ambani’s vantara said. The order has laid down several conditions, including that madhuri cannot be used in processions or for any other purpose.

Article Title: Decade on, disability policy rejig in limbo
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ten years after the current disability law was passed, govt is yet to frame a revised National Policy for Persons with Disabilities. The existing National Policy for Persons with Disabilities was adopted 20 years ago."This prolonged delay is particularly concerning because a contemporary national policy is essential to translate the rights guaranteed under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPDA) Act, 2016 and India's commitments under UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities into a coordinated, measurable and adequately resourced whole-of-govt framework," stated the organisation, Doctors with Disabilities: Agents of Change (DwDAoC), in its letter to the minister for social justice and empowerment and secretary of Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD).Govt had acknowledged the need for a new national policy in its 2022 public notice inviting comments on the draft policy. The task force constituted to draft the policy had submitted the draft on Oct 12, 2021, and the deadline for stakeholder comments was Sept 30, 2022. Four years after the consultation process, India continues to operate under the national policy formulated in 2006, pointed out the letter.When drafting the new policy, the department explicitly acknowledged the significant developments since 2006, including India's ratification of the UN convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, enactment of RPDA, 2016, and adoption of National Education Policy, 2020.In 2016, RPDA replaced Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995. "As an organisation led by and representing health professionals with disabilities, we are particularly concerned about the gaps that arise when disability policy is not effectively integrated across health, social protection and other sectors. The medicalisation of disability in professional assessment and eligibility has also been challenged . .. These judgments underscore the need to move decisively towards a rights-based, functional and accommodation-oriented approach rather than one that treats disability itself as a proxy for incapacity," stated DwDAoC founder Dr Satendra Singh in his letter.The letter pointed out several shortcomings in the draft national policy including the lack of adequate convergence with health ministry's proposed accessibility standards for healthcare and how accessibility requirements for goods and services remained inadequately reflected in public procurement frameworks.The organisation sought the current status of the revised national policy, reasons for its delay, whether a revised draft had been prepared following consultations, the proposed mechanism and timeline for further consultation, if any, and the expected date by which the revised national policy would be notified.
Article Summary: The existing national policy for persons with disabilities was adopted 20 years ago. Govt had acknowledged the need for a new national policy in its 2022 public notice inviting comments on the draft policy. The task force constituted to draft the policy had submitted the draft on oct 12, 2021, and the deadline for stakeholder comments was sept 30, 2022.

Article Title: For governance draft, MHA asks Ladakh bodies to answer 7 queries
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Ladakh outfits in talks with the home ministry on safeguards for the Union territory, have been asked to come up with a draft proposal addressing seven key questions relating to the larger governance structure for Ladakh, including the division of powers and functions between the proposed UT-level body and the seven district councils.Sources involved in the ongoing dialogue process between the home ministry and Ladakh administration on one side and the Leh Apex Body (LAB), Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) and activist Sonam Wangchuk, on the other, told TOI that the latest round on Sept 9 saw a presentation being made by the MHA on different aspects of the proposed governance structure involving the three tiers, the apex UT-level body, autonomous district councils and the panchayats.The first question sought suggestions on the name of the UT-level legislative body as well as its executive arm. A key angle discussed was the proposed representation of LAHDC representatives in the UT-level body. The Ladakh representatives were asked if they favour direct elections to the UT-level legislative body, with the members representing different constituencies to be carved through delimitation. The LAHDC would thus have no direct representation in the UT-level body.Alternatively, it was proposed that the UT-level body may be indirectly elected by the LAHDCs. A consensus emerged in favour of direct elections.As for the district councils, they will also have direct elections, as per the process already followed for the existing two councils in Ladakh and Kargil.The third question focused on functions that should necessarily be exercised by the UT-level body “in the interest of uniformity, coordinated development and effective administration”. The MHA officials assured that the UT-level body would be given charge of matters related to land, culture and heritage, environment, mineral resources as well as those covered under Article 240 of the Constitution of India.The Ladakh representatives were asked what functions should remain at the district level, so as to protect local interests and ensure responsive governance. Also, they were asked to specify what principles should guide the allocation of powers between the UT-level body and LAHDCs; the options being local preference, administrative efficiency and uniformity of policy.Another poser to LAB, KDA and Wangchuk related to subjects that should fall within the law-making domain of the UT-level elected body, which shall be in tune with the basis structure of the Constitution.The Ladakh bodies were told to submit their answers to the seven queries so that a draft proposal could be prepared for the next round of discussions likely in October. Since the proposed governance structure is expected to be a unique model, legal opinion will have to be taken before finalising the legislative framework.Notwithstanding the progress made in the Sept 9 discussions, LAB, KDA and Wangchuk had expressed disappointment with the lack of “headway” in the discussions, a day later. When contacted, Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra disagreed and insisted that the talks were productive, with the entire legislative process of creation of the UT-level body as well as autonomous councils in the five new Ladakh districts, explained in detail to the Ladakh representatives. They were told that a Constitutional amendment would have to be passed by Parliament along with a separate legislation detailing the powers and responsibilities of different tiers of the proposed governance structure.“Clarity was offered on the proposed constitutional safeguards. Besides, an assurance was given to the Ladakh bodies that their demand for withdrawal of cases related to the violent events of September 24, 2025 as well as compensation would be put up before the Ladakh LG,” said Kundra.The LG, in fact, accepted the demand on Sunday, announcing a compensation of Rs 15 lakh each to the next kin of those killed, Rs 3 lakh for those who sustained minor injuries and Rs 1 lakh for ones with minor injuries.While all other Ladakh representatives sounded positive at the end of the Sept 9 talks, Wangchuk is said to have demanded that no major decisions regarding the proposed powers of the UT-level body be taken till it is in place.This demand was however rejected by MHA which reminded him that the Ladakh LG was empowered by the Constitution to take decisions related to administration and governance, and that there could not be a void.Sources in Ladakh govt indicated that not all Ladakh representatives may be on the same page on the call to revive the agitation in view of the “failure” of Sept 9 talks. “The prime mover of the agitation plan is Wangchuk; the others are not in favour of a belligerent approach and prefer to build on the progress achieved in the talks so far,” said an officer.
Article Summary: Ladakh outfits in talks with the home ministry on safeguards for the union territory. They have been asked to come up with a draft proposal addressing seven key questions relating to the larger governance structure for ladakh. These include the division of powers and functions between the proposed ut-level body and the seven district councils.

Article Title: Ladakh begins reviving Tso Kar glacial lake
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: To revive the rapidly shrinking Tso Kar glacial lake, Ladakh administration has launched a project to divert an average of 132 cusecs (around 320 million litres) of untapped glacier water daily from Rupsho Kharnak stream in Changthang district to the lake. Officials expect the lake will be restored to its former glory within a year, calling it the first project of its scale in India to revive a high-altitude lake under such harsh climatic conditions.Situated at an altitude of nearly 15,000ft, the lake has lost nearly 70% of its water over the past decade, shrinking from around 11,000 acres to just 3,200 acres. Once a thriving habitat for migratory birds, including the black-necked crane, it now attracts far fewer birds.The project follows the successful diversion of 90 million litres of Stok glacier water into irrigation canals in Igoo-Phey and Chuchot villages near Leh. The administration described it as the region’s second major water-management initiative of its kind.The revival was conceived after Lt Governor VK Saxena visited Tso Kar on Aug 10. Villagers told him the lake once supported centuries-old salt trade and maintained a delicate ecological balance, but its decline had resulted in loss of grazing land and shrinking bird populations.Saxena directed the public health engineering department to survey the area. Its report, submitted on Aug 30 after 15 days of groundwork, proposed an 11km RCC channel. Saxena, however, ruled out a new RCC structure and suggested first diverting the water to a depression through a simple earthen channel. Work began on Sept 2, ahead of the winter freeze.Rupsho Kharnak stream, located about 11km from Tso Kar at an altitude of 18,000ft, has a peak summer discharge of around 132 cusecs. So far, 20 cusecs is being diverted to the first depression, which has filled by about 20% in four days using an earthen channel and a defunct concrete canal built in 1995.Before reaching Tso Kar, water will fill three natural depressions, creating freshwater wetlands of 270, 24 and 10 acres with a combined capacity of nearly 1,230 million litres. The wetlands will allow sediments to settle, ensuring cleaner water reaches the lake, while also creating new habitats for migratory birds and potential tourist attractions visible from Leh-Manali highway.
Article Summary: Tso kar has lost nearly 70% of its water over the past decade, shrinking from around 11,000 acres to just 3,200 acres. Officials expect the lake will be restored to its former glory within a year. The project follows the successful diversion of 90 million litres of stok glacier water into irrigation canals.

Article Title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami encourages youth participation in shaping 'developed Uttarakhand by 2047' at 'Mukhyamantri Yuva Vidyarthi Manthan'
Article Text:
Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday participated in the 'Mukhyamantri Yuva Vidyarthi Manthan'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday participated in the 'Mukhyamantri Yuva Vidyarthi Manthan' programme, organised on the theme 'Mere Sapno Ka Uttarakhand' at the auditorium located at the Chauras campus of Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University.During the programme, the Chief Minister held a direct interaction with students from across the state and sought to understand their views, suggestions, aspirations and vision for a developed Uttarakhand. He also addressed their queries and guided them on various issues, according to a press release.CM Dhami said the energy, ideas and commitment of students towards building a developed Uttarakhand were encouraging. He said empowering the younger generation to become self-reliant, aware and responsible citizens was among the state government's priorities.He said the ideas and suggestions of young people could play an important role in determining the direction of Uttarakhand's development. "The students of today will lead Uttarakhand and India tomorrow," he said.The Chief Minister said the 'Mere Sapno Ka Uttarakhand' campaign had received an overwhelming response from students across the state, with 2,67,744 students submitting essays and their ideas under the campaign.He said the ideas expressed by the students reflected their vision, sensitivity and commitment towards the development, prosperity and bright future of Uttarakhand. Appreciating their essays, Dhami said all the students had expressed their thoughts so well that it was difficult to decide who had written well and who had written exceptionally well, the press release said.During the interaction, Seema Semwal, a Class 11 student from Rudraprayag, spoke about her essay on migration. She told the Chief Minister that she had written the essay in two to three days and chose migration as the topic because she had experienced the issue herself.Dhami said there were primarily two types of migration in Uttarakhand, permanent and temporary. He said moving out of one's home for education and employment was not always negative, as studying, learning and gaining experience elsewhere provided young people with better exposure.However, he acknowledged the difficulties faced by women in the hill areas. Despite challenging circumstances, he said, mothers and sisters in the hills continued to manage their families and communities while working themselves and inspiring others, the release said.Shreya Semwal, a student from Devprayag, shared her views on the theme 'Pahad Rahein, Apne Rahein, Mere Sapne Rahein', highlighting the need to expand employment and opportunities in the hills while remaining connected to one's roots.Priya, a student of Pauri's Government Engineering College, also shared her vision for a developed Uttarakhand. The Chief Minister said a developed India could only be built when every village, district and state became part of the mainstream of development.Student Tamanna highlighted migration and low income from agriculture, saying, "My mountains, my employment; employment will be created even on the rocky terrain." Appreciating her thought, Dhami said it reflected a positive mindset.He said circumstances could be challenging, but the resolve to achieve something better in life should remain strong. He urged the youth of Uttarakhand to move forward with the aim of turning challenges into opportunities.Student Srishti raised questions about people's trust in government schools and hospitals. Responding to her, the Chief Minister said personalities such as APJ Abdul Kalam and Prime Minister Narendra Modi had risen from ordinary families to occupy the highest positions in the country.He said young people had an important role to play in improving systems. The present generation, he said, understood what was good and better, and students should remain aware of development works and various systems in their districts and the state and contribute towards bringing about positive change, the release said.Anushka, a student from Rudraprayag, shared her views on preventing migration. Dhami said the geographical conditions of Uttarakhand were challenging, but the government was working to provide electricity, water and other basic facilities in villages across the state.He said much more remained to be done, and the government was continuously working in this direction. The Chief Minister said more than 500 smart classes were currently operational in the state and reverse migration was also taking place.As per the release, the Chief Minister urged the youth not to remain merely job seekers but to aim at becoming job creators.Ishika Negi and Gaurav Bisht shared suggestions related to tourism, environmental conservation and the Char Dham pilgrimage. Students also expressed their views on protecting Uttarakhand's natural resources while linking tourism with employment generation and the local economy.Student Mukesh Kushwaha suggested extending facilities such as helicopter ambulances to small villages to improve healthcare access and providing skill-development training at the school level.Calling the suggestion important, Dhami said the government's endeavour was to provide young people with the necessary facilities and opportunities to make the best use of their talent and capabilities. He said continuous efforts were being made to make youth self-reliant through skill development and employment-oriented education.The Chief Minister said all the ideas and suggestions put forward by the students should be taken seriously. He said every individual had an important role in building a developed India and a developed Uttarakhand.He also urged the youth to stay away from drugs and channelise their energy in a positive direction while ensuring their active participation in nation-building.Dhami said the day was special for him as he had the opportunity to interact directly with students. Their views, he said, reflected their vision, knowledge, sensitivity and thoughts about the future, the release said.He said all the students demonstrated a strong desire to move forward and achieve something better. This energy, he said, was the greatest strength in building a developed Uttarakhand.The Chief Minister said the youth were the future of the country and that the Uttarakhand and India of tomorrow would be shaped by their dreams, resolve and hard work.He said it was important to understand what India should look like in 2047, what contribution the youth should make, what role they should play and how systems should function. The participation and vision of young people on these issues, he said, were extremely important.Dhami said every young person had a significant role in the development journey and urged them to turn their dreams into goals and continue moving forward with determination.The Chief Minister said young people from Uttarakhand were performing well in various fields. He said initiatives such as the Mukhyamantri Yuva Yojana were being undertaken to promote the talent of youth in technology and innovation, the release said.He also said the state government had enacted strict laws against those involved in examination malpractice and cheating, ensuring that meritorious youth received transparent and fair opportunities.During the programme, student Aditi Gautam presented a painting made by her to Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami.Teacher and nodal officer Ankush was honoured for ensuring better participation in the programme. Rudraprayag District Magistrate Vishal Mishra was also honoured for ensuring 100 per cent participation of students from the district in the essay competition.The Chief Minister extended his best wishes to the students and urged them to make their dreams their goals, work hard consistently and utilise their talent and energy in the development of the state and the country, the release said.He said the Uttarakhand of the future would be the Uttarakhand of the dreams of its youth, and every young person in the state would have an important role in building it.
Article Summary: Pushkar singh dhami on sunday participated in the 'mukhyamantri yuva vidyarthi manthan' programme, organised on the theme 'mere sapno ka uttarakhand' chief minister held a direct interaction with students from across the state and sought to understand their views, suggestions and aspirations.

Article Title: Mamata's TMC faction names candidates for Nandigram, Rejinagar bypolls in Bengal
Article Text:
TMC names Sanchita Pradhan, Rabiul Alam Chowdhury candidates for Nandigram, Rejinagar bypolls

NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress (TMC) faction led by Mamata Banerjee on Sunday announced Sanchita Pradhan (Dey) and Rabiul Alam Chowdhury as its candidates for the October 6 bypolls to the Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats, respectively. The counting of votes is set to take place on October 9.Pradhan is a new face, while Chowdhury is a former MLA, news agency PTI reports.The announcement comes after an earlier rebel TMC faction said it would support Mamata Banerjee, strengthening the party's position ahead of the bypolls.The Nandigram bypoll was necessitated after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari vacated the seat and chose to retain Bhabanipur, where he defeated TMC chief Mamata Banerjee in the Assembly elections held earlier this year. The Rejinagar seat fell vacant after Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) founder Humayun Kabir resigned from the seat, having also won from Nowda.The two seats are expected to witness a keen political contest, with the bypoll results likely to be closely watched ahead of the next electoral battle in the state.
Article Summary: Tmc names sanchita pradhan, rabiul alam chowdhury candidates for nandigram, rejinagar bypolls. The counting of votes is set to take place on october 9. The announcement comes after an earlier rebel tmc faction said it would support mamata banerjee.

Article Title: How Gujarat's villagers turned mangroves into a natural coastal shield
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In the 1980s, when much of Gujarat’s coastline was losing its mangrove cover, some coastal communities began protecting the few patches that remained. What looked like a small act of conservation would eventually become part of one of India’s most striking mangrove recoveries.Government data shows just how dramatic that transformation has been.According to the Forest Survey of India (FSI), Gujarat had around 427 sq km of mangrove cover in 1987. By 1999, that figure had more than doubled to 1,031 sq km. It reached 1,164.06 sq km in 2023, making Gujarat home to nearly one-quarter of India's mangrove cover. In 2026, the cover has grown to 1177.27 sq km.It attributes the growth to a combination of large-scale plantation programmes, public-private partnerships, community participation and better protection of existing forests.Mangroves are much more than trees growing in salty mud.Their dense network of roots holds sediment together, reduces coastal erosion and slows waves and storm surges before they can reach settlements further inland. The forests also provide breeding and nursery grounds for fish, crabs and other marine species, making them important to both coastal ecosystems and livelihoods.The numbers also reveal how significant Gujarat's recovery has become.The state's 1,164 sq km of mangroves in 2023 accounted for 23.66% of India's entire mangrove cover, second only to West Bengal.But the recovery has not been a simple story of trees being planted by the government. In several parts of Gujarat, conservation efforts have involved coastal communities in protecting and regenerating mangrove areas. That local involvement matters because mangroves occupy a difficult landscape — one constantly shaped by tides, salinity, grazing, cutting and human activity.The government has now taken the approach nationwide through MISHTI, launched in 2023 to restore and promote mangrove ecosystems along India's coast. Under the programme, mangroves are increasingly being treated as natural infrastructure — ecosystems that can perform some of the protective functions that would otherwise require expensive coastal engineering.Gujarat's story therefore offers an unusual lesson in climate protection: sometimes the most effective coastal defence is not something built against the sea.It is something that grows between the land and the sea.And in Gujarat, decades after villagers began protecting those seemingly insignificant patches of mangrove, they have grown into forests spanning more than 1,100 sq km — forming a vast, living barrier along one of India's most exposed coastlines.
Article Summary: Gujarat's 1,164 sq km of mangroves in 2023 accounted for 23.66% of india's entire mangrove cover, second only to west bengal. Government attributes growth to plantation programmes, public-private partnerships, community participation and better protection of existing forests.

Article Title: Amit Shah vows to implement UCC in all 21 NDA-ruled states before 2029
Article Text:
Union home minister Amit Shah

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the BJP-led NDA government would implement the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in all 21 states under its rule before 2029, asserting that the code had already been introduced in several states.“We introduced the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in several states. I am confident that we will implement the UCC in all 21 states governed by the BJP-led NDA before 2029,” Shah said while addressing a press conference in Mumbai.Shah also said the government’s response to terrorism had been marked by a policy of zero tolerance, citing the surgical strikes, air strikes and Operation Sindoor.“Operations such as the surgical strikes, air strikes, and Operation Sindoor have established a policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, while security has been prioritized across various sectors,” he said.The Uniform Civil Code (UCC) proposes a common set of personal laws for all citizens, covering matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance and adoption, irrespective of religion. It aims to ensure equality before the law and promote national integration by replacing religion-based personal laws with a uniform legal framework.Shah also said a month-long “Seva Sankalp Abhiyan” to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 25 years of public service will be conducted nationwide from September 17 to October 17.The campaign will cover every district, Lok Sabha and Assembly constituency, as well as every polling booth.Shah said the entire NDA alliance, voluntary organisations and people across the country will participate in the campaign. He said the initiative will coincide with PM Modi’s birthday on September 17 and mark the completion of 25 years of his tenure as Chief Minister and Prime Minister on October 6, 2026.The campaign will focus on taking the message of service, good governance, welfare of the poor and a developed India to the booth level, rather than being limited to a series of events.The campaign’s main attraction will be a bike yatra from Kashi to Vadnagar in Gujarat. The yatra will begin on September 17, PM Modi’s birthday, after water from 10 rivers is offered at the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, and will conclude around 20 days later, on October 7, in his birthplace Vadnagar.
Article Summary: Union home minister amit shah says uniform civil code (ucc) will be implemented before 2029. Shah also said a month-long “seva sankalp abhiyan’ to mark prime minister narendra modi’s 25 years of public service will be conducted nationwide from september 17 to october 17.
